message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit price of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$9,812 total — within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, and the limit was set just above the $222.70 last / $222.72 ask so it was close to market). The case for buying: Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024) revenue came in at $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and full fiscal 2024 results reported in its 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) showed total net sales of $391.0 billion, net income of $93.7 billion, diluted EPS of $6.08 (including a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge), and operating cash flow of $118.3 billion — a highly cash-generative business with returning growth. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were roughly flat around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual rollout of Apple Intelligence, which suggests expectations are not stretched and leaves optionality around the AI upgrade cycle. I sized the position at just under the per-order cap given the mixed near-term demand signals (China/iPhone 16 uncertainty) and kept the order as a single limit buy, with no money moved out of the account (cash was $50,000; MSFT position untouched).
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 223.00, 44 shares = $9,812. Under $10k per order, total today $9,812 < $20k. Good.

Summarize.
